newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tel Aviv bourse delays decision on trading system.
newsitem.headline: Tel Aviv bourse delays decision on trading system.

text.p: The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) will make a final decision on when it will launch its computerised continuous trading system by the middle of next week, the exchange's spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"We are at the moment conducting extensive testing that is supposed to solve all the network problems we have encountered," spokeswoman Etti Tutnauer said.

The TASE's board of directors was supposed to approve a date for the new trading system on Thursday. But instead the board decided it would let officials fix a date next week based on further test results, Tutnauer said.

She said the system would probably be introduced in mid- to late July. "We are now testing the communications sytem between us and the members," she said. "After that we'll do about eight weeks of test trading."
Ester Levanon, executive vice-president for information systems and administration at TASE, had said earlier this week that the new system would probably be introduced in late June or early July.
Levanon attributed the delay to TASE's decision to widen the system to enable commercial banks to relay trading information through their computer networks to branches around the country.
The new system will initially be used to trade about 10 stocks from the Mishtanim list of top 100 shares and after a month of trials expanded to the blue chip shares of the Maof 25 index, she said.
TASE now uses a system it calls "semi-continuous trading" for its heavy capitalisation shares. The new system is aimed at making the TASE more closely resemble trading systems elsewhere in the world.
